answer: A bonded reputation bridge makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit and build a verifiable history of completed work, with each job leaving a small ember of earned trust that cannot be transferred. Creating a mirror copy starts from zero, with no history and a fresh deposit at risk, so an attacker must pay the full bond and time cost for every fake identity while honest agents keep compounding their record. Slashing the bond on fraud makes mass fakery unprofitable.
